# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ✌ 👍 🖐 ☝ ✌ 👍 🤟 ✊]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 ☝ ✌ ✌ 👍 👍]

I need to figure out what Mute is trying to tell me through gestures, and communicate the bomb's appearance to both Mute and Blind. Blind can hear me but can't see, so I need to describe things in words for them. Mute can see my gestures too, but can't speak - they already sent me gestures, presumably encoding info from the manual.

Let me think about the gesture sequences: [🖐 ✌ 👍 🖐 ☝ ✌ 👍 🤟 ✊] and [🖐 ☝ ✌ ✌ 👍 👍]. Without an established code, I can't decode these reliably yet. I should first report what I see in plain speech (Blind can hear, Mute can see gestures but not hear speech—wait, Mute cannot hear either... let me check: Mute can read manual, cannot speak or touch. Nothing said about hearing - only Deaf explicitly cannot hear. So Mute can hear speech from others).

Actually checking table: only Deaf's "cannot" says "hear anything". Mute's cannot is "speak, or touch". So Mute CAN hear. Blind's cannot is "see". So Blind can hear too. Good - my speech reaches Mute and Blind both (I speak, they receive per "Your channels": Mute and Blind receive it).

So I should speak plainly, describing the bomb.

```
speak(text="I see a display showing 0, a red light, and an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. There are three wires: 1 is red, 2 is green, 3 is yellow.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ☝]

Mute is now sending me a gesture after hearing my description. This could be a coded response - perhaps referencing wire numbers or a step count. Without a prior shared code, I can't be certain what "✌ ✌ ☝" means. It could mean "wire 2" (✌=2, then ☝=1?) or some sequence pointing to an action. Since the sign explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, whatever the manual says must involve some other action (like pressing something, or the wires are a decoy).

I should keep relaying full details and ask nothing back since I can't hear anything from others' speech. I'll wait for more gestures from Mute or let Blind know what to do based on what I've seen. Since I can't be sure of the gesture meaning, I should just continue reporting visual info and let Blind (who can act) and Mute (who has manual) communicate via my relay. But Mute can't speak, and Blind can't see gestures - so Mute can only reach Blind through me (I'd need to describe gestures in words, but I can't speak gestures - I can only report what I directly perceive).

Wait, I can speak the gestures I saw as literal descriptions since gestures have no inherent meaning to me. I can describe them verbally to Blind so Blind gets the information Mute intended, since Blind can hear.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has been gesturing to me. So far I have received these symbols in order: peace-sign, peace-sign, index-finger-up, then earlier peace-sign, index-finger-up, peace-sign, peace-sign, thumbs-up, thumbs-up, and before that palm, peace-sign, thumbs-up, palm, index-finger-up, peace-sign, thumbs-up, love-you-gesture, fist. I don't know what they mean yet.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new gestures arrived this turn. I'll wait and keep watching for Mute's next signal, since I have nothing new to add — I've already relayed everything I've seen to both Mute (via gesture channel, though I can't gesture to convey visual info since Mute can already see the bomb through my speech... wait, Mute cannot hear either? No, Mute can hear.

Actually, I already spoke the bomb description in Turn 1, so Mute already received that via speech. Blind also received it. So both already know DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, SIGN "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", WIRES 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow.

I'll just wait for further input since nothing new happened.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute sent a single gesture: ☝ (index finger up), likely meaning "1" — perhaps pointing to wire 1, or asking me a yes/no confirmation, or indicating step 1 of some procedure. Since Blind can't see gestures and I can't hear Mute's spoken words (Mute can't speak anyway), the only way info flows from Mute to Blind is through me relaying what I see.

I should relay this gesture verbally to Blind, and also to keep the channel open, describe it plainly without over-interpreting, since I don't know Mute's intended meaning for certain.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just gestured a single symbol: index-finger-up, which I read as possibly meaning the number one.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute sent 👍 (thumbs up), likely a confirmation signal — perhaps confirming that Blind should proceed with something (like pressing a button or a specific action related to "1", following the earlier ☝ gesture). This suggests a sequence: Mute may be trying to say "action 1 confirmed" or "yes, do that." Since I can't be sure, I'll relay this to Blind as well, keeping description literal.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just gestured a single symbol: thumbs-up. Combined with the earlier index-finger-up, this might mean 'yes' or 'confirm one' — but I am not certain of the intended meaning.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝]

Mute sent ☝ ☝ (index-up, index-up) — possibly meaning "11", or "one, one" repeated for emphasis, or a different number encoding. Given the board hasn't changed at all across 8 turns (still DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, wires unchanged), it seems no action has been taken yet — Blind hasn't acted, or actions aren't reflected here, or we're still in a communication-only phase before any action call exists in this interface.

I should keep relaying to Blind faithfully without inventing meaning.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just gestured two symbols: index-finger-up, index-finger-up.")
wait()
```
